newsitem.title: USA: Network Peripherals to expand products.
newsitem.headline: Network Peripherals to expand products.

text.p: Network Peripherals Inc, looking for new sources of growth, said Monday it will expand its line of Ethernet computer networking switches to include gear for the small to mid-size company markets.

The new products, to be introduced late this year, will let Network Peripherals tap a $5 billion market that is expected to grow about 35 percent a year for the rest of the decade, said Pauline Lo Alker, president and chief executive.
"We believe the current products can only address a portion of the market," Alker told Reuters. "This way, would look to turn our road map" to squarely take advantage of the market.

Network Peripherals, based in Milpitas, Calif., makes most of its money selling adapter cards, which are relatively inexpensive devices for connecting personal computers to networks. The company intends to expand its line of switches, which are more expensive standalone devices for handling communication between PCs.
By the end of the year, the company will expand its NuSwitch line with an additional family of products based on so-called Fast Ethernet and Gigabit Ethernet technologies, Alker said.
She declined to estimate by how much she expects the company's revenue to increase.
